Karthik / team — draft answers for SAST/DAST and SBOM below. I attached a short SAST-summary and the latest DAST snapshot. Please review and flag edits.

SAST (development pipeline):
- Tools: we run CodeQL (enterprise) for repo-wide analysis and Semgrep for PR gating. We also use internal heuristics for secret scanning.
- Cadence: PR gating for all repos (blocking for high-confidence findings), full repository scans nightly on master branches, and weekly incremental scans for services in production.
- Triage: findings triaged automatically into Jira (SUP-7892) with severity mapping (low/med/high/critical) and false-positive suppression workflows.
- False positive rate: our combination of CodeQL + tuning yields a <10% false positive rate on high severity findings after tuning.

DAST (runtime scanning):
- Environment: DAST runs against staging clusters isolated from production (mirror of production traffic).
- Tools: combination of open-source (OWASP ZAP) and commercial scanners for authenticated app flows; authenticated scans executed using ephemeral test credentials.
- Cadence: weekly DAST suites against staging for services with public endpoints and nightly quick checks for freshly deployed services.
- Remediation: verified findings create Jira tickets; DAST results are cross-referenced against SAST findings to reduce duplication.

SBOM and build pipeline:
- Formats: we generate CycloneDX and SPDX outputs from our build pipeline (Maven/Gradle and NPM).
- Delivery: can export per-build SBOMs and aggregate component inventories. We can push SBOM artifacts to an SFTP endpoint on a configurable cadence (daily/weekly) or share via secure Drive link.
- Scope: SBOMs include dependency version, package URL (purl), and license metadata; we can offer per-service CSV export (attached: SBOM-everstone-20261110.csv).

Attachments: SAST-summary-2026.pdf, DAST-results-Q3-2026.pdf, SBOM-everstone-20261110.csv

Next: Markus, can you add the pen test cadence/exec summary and patch SLAs?

-Neha

Adding pen test and patching details — attaching redacted exec summary.

Pen testing:
- Cadence: annual third-party penetration test performed by accredited vendor (most recent completed 2026-08), plus targeted pen tests for major releases or changes in scope.
- Scope: network and application layer tests covering hosted API endpoints and our dedicated deployment tooling components. Internal scans cover privileged admin interfaces; customer-specific private deployments are included in scope for on-prem engagements as requested.
- Findings and remediation: critical and high findings are triaged immediately with remediation tickets and SLA expectations described below. We provide an executive summary with redactions for third-party reports (attached: pen-test-exec-summary-redacted.pdf).

Patch and CVE remediation SLAs (operational commitments vs. best-effort practice):
- Critical (e.g. RCE with weaponized PoC / active exploitation): target mitigation within 24 hours and patch deployment within 72 hours where possible. Emergency out-of-band patches and rollback plans are used for critical incidents.
- High (remote exploit without evidence of active exploitation): target mitigation 72 hours; patching in next scheduled maintenance window if immediate patch not available, with compensating controls until patching completed.
- Medium: remediation and patching within 7 calendar days for exploitable issues; tracked with SLA target of 14 days for lower impact mediums as operational practice.
- Low: scheduled remediation with 30-day standard window.

Escalation and exception process:
- If remediation cannot meet SLA, the owner escalates to Security Operations and the CISO review board; exceptions are time-boxed and documented.
- We maintain audit logs of exceptions and remediation steps; these are available in redwood's customer portal on request.

Tracking and evidence:
- All findings and remediation tracked in Jira (SUP-7892). We provide summarized metrics per-quarter and can provide CSV exports for audits.

-Markus
